statements.text: Deep fakes and other AI-generated content is making it difficult to discern facts, discern truth — that’s going to be more present in our lives. And so we need to create a policy that adequately moves in the direction of avoiding problems that lie ahead.

In my view, Congress must play an active role in ensuring that we sufficiently address challenges & explore opportunities of artificial intelligence.

Glad I could join @RepDonBeyer & EU partners with @RegulatingAI today for a roundtable discussion on the path forward for action. https://t.co/4Z2VlfdjfG

Federal funding for the AI Safety Institute is crucial to helping develop evaluations for AI systems.

During today's @ScienceDems hearing, I asked @NIST Director Dr. Locascio how @CommerceGov funding cuts would impact the agency’s ability to establish AI safety standards. https://t.co/XfvIfOGRj8

Congratulations to all the students who completed the HASTE workshop today at @brownu Data-thon!

By opening doors of opportunity for students interested in science, we ensure that tomorrow’s leaders are well-equipped to engage in the rapidly changing future of AI in health care. https://t.co/7YJxK6V2V8

Great to join many leaders in our community at the @ProvChamber today for the annual Congressional Breakfast.

From AI to foreign affairs to infrastructure, we discussed so much that I’m optimistic we can find solutions for with the right leadership in Washington. https://t.co/7TiCI3jzAA

The impact of artificial intelligence will only continue to grow as more people use the technology. 
 
I’m proud to work with @congressmankean on the LIFT AI Act, bipartisan legislation to invest in — and expand — AI literacy education in the classroom.

https://t.co/x4Y6FZ8Cfv

AI is going to be more and more important to us in every dimension of our lives. [...] The purpose of this legislation is to make sure that we have a comprehensive learning and understanding of what AI is, to make sure that we’re unlocking its power for good. And a lot of that starts in the classroom.
What we need to figure out is how we deploy it for good

Thank you to the leaders & experts in our state who joined us for a roundtable discussion on AI at Smithfield High School today!

Through a collaborative approach, we can work to unlock the immense potential of artificial intelligence to benefit every student in every community. https://t.co/GZNOUCUoFp

Thanks to my partnership w/ @CongressmanKean, our bipartisan LIFT AI Bill just advanced through the @HouseScience Committee!

After speaking with educators and students in RI, it is clear we must teach the next generation to use artificial intelligence responsibly & effectively. https://t.co/sTuhrsQ0Fy
As we all know, AI isn’t far off in the future. It’s here. It’s now. And, it’s having an impact on our school systems and educators.

statements.text: We need to name the problem. Problem identification is how you get to a solution. Having the right people at the table and setting broad goals around inclusion are crucial to harnessing AI’s potential in areas like public health and education.

statements.text: The best thing we can do is isolate the noise, focus on objectivity, and ensure clear alignment on truth and facts. With responsible AI development, we can build a future where technology enhances democracy rather than undermines it.

statements.text:
In our @Sciencedems hearing today, I discussed how investing in domestic research is key to beating China in the AI innovation race. 

Unfortunately, the Trump administration seems to be rowing in the wrong direction. 

By canceling STEM research grants to fund AI training and deporting international students, Trump is threatening our country’s ability to compete.

Joined in Rumford with @SenJackReed to see @HavocAi_USV’s next gen autonomous marine vessel prototype. Right on the Seekonk River, they’re marrying AI and marine technologies for commercial and defense use.

Future thinking companies like this are becoming integral to our #BlueEconomy.

Trump's siding with the demands of big tech and billionaires that will profit over the people who could get hurt.

His AI executive order will stop actions to keep Americans safe.

Right now, our laws do not explicitly cover the remote access of technologies via network connections, including the internet or cloud computing services. H.R. 2683 would close this gap by giving the Bureau of Industry and Security statutory authority to control the remote access of items by bad actors who aim to jeopardize our national security or foreign policy interests.
statements.context: House floor speech in support of H.R. 2683, the Remote Access Security Act, during debate on the bill.

statements.text:
Trump is handing our opponents our coordinates in the middle of a battle by selling China high-powered AI chips.

It puts our national security at risk.

But don't take it from me, take it from the experts who testified in front of @HouseForeign. https://t.co/M37AD9PTnD

Trump should not be selling our advanced AI chips to China.
 
He’s giving the advantage to an adversary, and I want to know why.
 
@RepGregoryMeeks and I demanded answers with @HouseForeign last week, and we'll keep up the drumbeat.

https://t.co/UzczvAkcnT

Joined @ITI_TechTweets for an important conversation on unlocking AI tools to keep small businesses and our future workforce from being left behind.

My LIFT AI Act makes sure schools, teachers & students can harness AI’s potential in the classroom. https://t.co/991kRs6AHu

Trump’s Sunday: AI slop portraying himself in image of Jesus? Attacking the Pope? Blasphemous.

Illegal wars of choice, cutting your health care & raising your gas prices. Immoral.

It should be very clear that we can — and should be — united on opposing this nonsense and havoc. https://t.co/bmQCAT05oq

statements.text:
Went to @sciencedems briefing with frontier AI companies. 

It’s abundantly clear: AI is moving too fast & we need to regulate.

There’s no time for delay.

Congress must take immediate action to keep Americans safe. https://t.co/7P0xoAhCTV

Speaker Johnson sent the House home early.

That means House Republicans have cancelled 63 total days instead of working in D.C. to:

💰Lower costs
🖥️Regulate AI
❌Stop Trump’s illegal war

Enough avoiding big issues. Let’s focus on helping Americans. https://t.co/IIY0atmCMM

A powerful AI CEO was being honeypotted by a Chinese spy. 

Trump kept selling that CEO’s chips abroad anyway.

Americans deserve answers about why shady dealers are allowed to buy the most powerful AI chips in the world.

Time for accountability, Trump.
https://t.co/7qOEmEpnJQ

Trump let American AI chips fall into the hands of shady companies & did nothing about a powerful AI CEO compromised by his affair with a Chinese spy.

We need answers.

Why is Trump shipping chips overseas? Why risk our national security? What's in it for him? 👀 https://t.co/qD2k4uj76P
Now, Trump must crack down on advanced chip exports before he hands our AI advantage to an adversary.

We call on the Department of Commerce to immediately halt exports of advanced artificial intelligence chips to the People’s Republic of China (PRC) amid recent reporting about PRC intelligence activities and of potential PRC access to these critical national security technologies. You cannot claim to be protecting American leadership in artificial intelligence while allowing our most advanced technology to reach a strategic competitor. National security must come before corporate sales targets.
